reasoning:
Let Z(n) = sum_{i>=1} floor(n/5^i) be the number of trailing zeros of n!. Z is nondecreasing and changes only at multiples of 5: Z(5m) - Z(5m-1) = v5(5m) >= 1. So the positive values attained by Z are exactly Z(5), Z(10), Z(15), ..., which are strictly increasing and hence distinct; a value k is skipped exactly when it falls strictly inside a jump of size v5(5m) >= 2, and each such jump skips v5(5m)-1 values.

Hence #attained positive k <= K equals the number of m >= 1 with Z(5m) <= K, i.e. floor(N/5) where N is the largest n with Z(n) <= K.

For K = 10000: Z(40000) = 8000+1600+320+64+12+2 = 9998; Z(40005) = 8001+1600+320+64+12+2 = 9999; Z(40010) = 8002+1600+320+64+12+2 = 10000; Z(40015) = 10001 > 10000. So N in [40010, 40014], floor(N/5) = 8002 attained values in 1..10000 (and k = 10000 itself is attained by 40010!).

Skipped count = 10000 - 8002 = 1998. Cross-check via jumps: sum over 5m <= 40010 of (v5(5m)-1) = Z(40010) - 40010/5 = 10000 - 8002 = 1998.
